_comment: klt erc supply spec for the composed floorplan stream
(layout/floorplan/trng_floorplan.gds, top cell trng_floorplan) -- the
whole-block power-delivery connectivity read, issue #447. Run it with
the pinned klt (signoff/check.py KLT_PIN):
klt erc layout/floorplan/trng_floorplan.gds \
layout/floorplan/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top trng_floorplan --format json --findings-only
layout/floorplan/floorplan.py (`--write` / the check path) pins the
response in reports/erc-supply.json to this spec and to the GDS by
content hash.
- `stackup`/`vias` follow layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json: stackup[0]
must carry role `gate` (klt erc's own contract), then Metal1-Metal5
with the contiguous Via1-Via4 chain. The inter-region trunks are drawn
on Metal4 with Metal3 risers (layout/floorplan/interregion.py), the
digital PDN reaches Metal5, and the analog regions are Metal1-Metal3.
- `label_layer`: 34/10 (standard-cell and ring Metal1 pin text), 36/10
(Metal2), 46/10 (the Metal4 trunk labels interregion.py draws, one per
net) and 81/10 (the digital PDN's Metal5 pin text).
- `nets[]`: the five region-level supply names the trunks carry, all
`kind: supply` so a short between any two is the severe
`erc.supply_short`. vddr1 and vddr2 are the two ring supplies, vdd the
combiner/sampler supply, vddd the digital supply, vss the one shared
ground. Each must resolve to exactly one electrical island.
- One spelling per physical supply. The cells inside a region label the
same island with other spellings (rings: cell-level `vddr`; digital
standard cells: `VDD`/`VSS` on 34/10) and the digital PDN adds
`vddd`/`vss` on 81/10. Declaring two spellings of one island as
separate supply nets would report that intentional aliasing as a false
`erc.supply_short` (see the digital spec), so only the trunk spelling
is declared; the other spellings are undeclared aliases and are not
asserted either way.
- NOT declared, deliberately: `vsubs`. The guard/substrate ring exists
only in the floorplan abstract and is kept separate from `vss`
(merging them is the `net.merged` failure documented in
interregion.py), so there is no label to declare and substrate
isolation from `vss` is not asserted by this spec.
- NOT declared: `ties[]`. The well-bias taps of the composed stream are
checked per region (the digital partition's spec declares them); the
analog regions draw no Nplus/Pplus/LVPWELL and give every PMOS a
floating well, so a composed tie declaration would be degenerate.
`ties_disclosure` in the report records this as `unexpressible`.

ties_disclosure.reason: No ties[] is declared and erc.missing_tie is not computed for the composed stream. The analog regions draw no Nplus/Pplus (31/0, 32/0) or LVPWELL (204/0) layer, so a well tap cannot be told from source/drain diffusion by layer, and their reference netlists give every PMOS a floating well; the digital partition's own spec (layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json) checks its tap sites. The substrate/guard-ring identity is likewise unverified here: no vsubs label exists in the stream and the guard ring is deliberately not merged into vss. Well-tie coverage and the substrate connection are unverified for the composed floorplan, not passed.
